summary: Iter30 acceptance for session-timeout fix (issue #1). All 5 new iter30 tests pass + 34/34 regression (iter17+21+22+23+multi_company_iso) still green. Demo token self-heals: db.user_sessions row deleted then GET /api/auth/me returns 200 with user_id 'user_demo_...', expires_at is ~30 days out and refreshes on every hit. OAuth rolling refresh verified: a manually-seeded session with 2-day expiry gets extended to ~7 days on first /auth/me hit, last_refreshed_at is populated, and the anti-thrash window blocks a second refresh within 4 minutes. Expired sessions (expires_at in the past) still 401 correctly. rca of the issue: Original bug: demo login button only worked while a pre-seeded db.user_sessions row (TTL ~7 days) was still alive; once expired/cleaned by a testing agent, users saw 'session expired' with no self-heal. Real Google OAuth sessions also had a hard 7-day cap with no extension, so long testing/data-entry sessions >15 min could hit intermittent 401s if cache/state cleared. Fix in /app/backend/auth.py: (1) DEMO_TOKEN constant + _ensure_demo_session() upserts a fresh 30-day session on every request bearing the demo token; (2) rolling refresh in get_current_user() bumps expires_at by +7d whenever session has <6d left AND last_refreshed_at is >4min old, preventing active users from being logged out. Verified end-to-end via pytest (delete row → auth/me 200) + Playwright (demo click → 4 protected routes + post-inactivity refetch).
